action_items.item: Route the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call page so a person is told when it fires.
Add a latency alert on io-pricing's basket-total endpoint, owned by checkout-platform.
Require every call io-shop makes to another service to have a test with a fake service that blocks, checking that the caller returns within a bound.
Have checkout-platform find out why io-pricing's basket-total calls slowed down from the onset until the restart.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers waited longer for io-shop's pages: the slowest requests, the ones the service's high-percentile response time tracks, took far longer than before, while failed requests stayed within their normal range.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release of io-shop: the production change events read for the day before the onset came back empty.
A feature flag change: the flag provider showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the investigation.

causal_chain.step: io-shop was waiting on io-pricing: from the onset, its calls to io-pricing for a shopper's basket total took about {G9feb.1} each. The log line counted between {G9feb.7} and {G9feb.8} such slow requests out of {G9feb.2} each minute, typically {G9feb.9}.
A slow io-pricing answer slowed the page because the account page calls `basket_total` inline and waits for the basket total with no time limit.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The shop's account page waits for a separate pricing service to work out the shopper's basket total, and it likely has no time limit on that wait, so when the pricing service slowed down the page slowed down too, even though it could have been shown without the total.

contributing_factors.factor: The HighLatency alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call person would have known about the slowdown as soon as the alert fired, and could have stepped in if restarting io-pricing had not brought the service back.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The record shows no alert on io-pricing's own latency. The slowdown was found only by io-shop's latency alert and then worked out from io-shop's slow-upstream-call log lines.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The slowdown would have been flagged at io-pricing itself and pointed straight at its owning team, instead of having to be worked out from io-shop's symptoms.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: io-shop's existing tests of the pricing call use fakes that answer straight away and only report a large `took_ms`, so the tests never exercised a pricing service that actually hangs.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test with a fake that blocks would have shown that the account page waits as long as io-pricing takes, so a time limit could have been added before io-pricing slowed down.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

got_lucky: Argus restarted io-pricing without knowing why it had slowed down, and the restart still brought the service back, which kept the slowdown short.

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent named one candidate, C1, which pointed at io-pricing, after reading the metrics, the production changes, the service register, the rollout state and the log lines.
The Mitigation Agent restarted io-pricing to act on C1.
The Mitigation Agent judged the restart confirmed after seeing that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent opened draft pull request #532 for a person to review.

input.root_cause: In the files Code-Fix read, io-shop's account page gets the basket total by calling io-pricing inline through `basket_total`, which waits however long the call takes and sets no time limit. The page already falls back to rendering without the total when the call raises `PricingServiceFailed`, but a slow call never raises, so however long io-pricing took was added straight onto the account page's response time.
input.still_at_risk: io-pricing could slow down again, and io-shop's account pages could slow down with it.
input.symptom: Shop pages loaded slowly for shoppers
